c.v: Built-up roofing

runs.v: is a low-slope membrane that alternates layers of reinforcing fabric and hot bitumen on the deck, then surfaces the plies with gravel, mineral granules, or a reflective coating. The multi-ply assembly shields the membrane from UV and impact.

c.v: Built-up roofing (BUR)

runs.v: is a multi-ply system for low-slope and flat roofs, the familiar tar-and-gravel roof, and it has been used on U.S. roofs for more than 100 years. BUR consists of alternating layers of bitumen and reinforcing fabrics, and the top layer is typically finished with gravel, mineral surfacing, or a protective coating: gravel set in the flood coat provides fire resistance and protects the bitumen against UV rays, and modern BUR systems may include reflective roof coatings to improve energy efficiency.

sections.heading: Common Built-Up Roofing Problems in West Orange, NJ

c.v: Ponding and drainage

runs.v: define the built-up roofing condition on West Orange's flat commercial corridors, because a low-slope roof requires at least one-quarter inch per foot of slope to drain. Ponding water held more than 48 hours counts as a defect that accelerates bitumen oxidation, per the NRCA and ARMA, so a Newark Quality Roofing scope maps the standing water and grades the deck to drain. Snow drifts and ice dams at scuppers and roof edges hold meltwater on the membrane through freeze-thaw cycles, and summer storms dump rain faster than a clogged drain carries it, so maintenance needs include regular inspections, in spring, in fall, and after major storms, and addressing issues like flashing failures or ponding water early.

c.v: Reservation-edge canopy

runs.v: off South Mountain and Eagle Rock drops leaves and branches onto the corridor roofs near West Orange's wooded edges, clogging drains, scuppers, and gutters and holding water on the membrane. A Newark Quality Roofing assessment clears the drainage path, reseals the failed flashing where water concentrates, and restores positive flow before the trapped moisture works between the plies.

c.v: Alligatoring and blistering

runs.v: mark a built-up roof at end of life, because the surfacing migrates and the bitumen plies oxidize across a 30-year service life, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, while blisters signal moisture trapped between the plies. A Newark Quality Roofing assessment resurfaces the sound membrane or specifies replacement once damage crosses 25–30% of the membrane, the flat-roof replacement threshold per Modernize and HomeGuide cost data.

c.v: Recover-versus-tear-off limits

runs.v: govern an aging BUR roof on a West Orange commercial or multi-family building, because full removal to the deck applies when the existing roof is water-soaked or already carries 2 or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 and the NJ Rehabilitation Subcode. sections.heading: NJ Roof Repair or Roof Replacement? The 25% Rule for Built-Up Roofs

c.v: What is the 25% rule for roofing?

runs.v: It has two meanings. As a rule of thumb, once damage covers about 25% of a roof, a full roof replacement usually costs less over time than repeated roof repair, and on a flat roof the line sits at 25–30% of the membrane. As an NJ roofing permit rule, commercial roofing requires a permit if over 25% of the roof area is repaired or replaced within 12 months, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 of the Uniform Construction Code, and the same applies to multi-family and attached buildings, while reroofing a detached one- or two-family house is ordinary maintenance, so a complete roof replacement requires no permit for detached homes.

sections.heading: Built-Up Roofing vs. Shingles and Other Roof Types

c.v: Are built-up roofs better than shingles?

runs.v: On a flat or low-slope roof, yes: built-up roofing is made for those roofs, while an asphalt shingle roof needs a slope of at least 2:12, with double underlayment up to 4:12, under the International Residential Code. On a pitched house roof, shingles win. Asphalt shingles typically last 20 to 30 years in West Orange, architectural asphalt shingles have a 30-year service life per the InterNACHI chart and can last 30 years or more, natural slate roofs can last 60 to 150 years when maintained, with slate installation at about $10 to $30 per square foot, and metal roofing systems can last 50 years or longer.

c.v: Flat roofing systems include EPDM, TPO, and modified bitumen options

runs.v: , plus PVC and BUR. TPO and PVC membranes reflect heat and tolerate ponding water, EPDM rubber is a cost-effective choice for low-traffic roofs, and modified bitumen systems add puncture resistance to commercial roofs; BUR earns its place where rooftop equipment and foot traffic call for multi-ply redundancy.

c.v: What are the disadvantages of a built-up roof?

runs.v: Weight comes first: gravel surfacing adds several hundred pounds per 100 square feet, so the deck and framing must carry it. Hot-mopped installation brings asphalt fumes and odor to an occupied building and goes slower than single-ply materials, a leak is harder to trace once water travels between plies, and loose gravel can clog drains.
